  A  
  Answer all the questions.  
  1A)          Students are given a task of designing an artificial cell membrane from the following two  
  molecules. Explain logically the questions related to designing of the cell membrane.  
  
  
  (4)  
  
  
  i) Which among the following molecules given is most likely to assemble and form a lipid  
  bilayer?  
  ii) What property of the molecule that is selected allows it to form a lipid bilayer?  
  iii) Which bond(s) or interaction(s) is/are most likely to stabilize the lipid bilayer?  
  iv) Illustrate the lipid bilayer structure in the aqueous environment by the selected molecule.  
  (1+1+1+1 = 4 marks)  
  
  1B)          Justify the reason for not having a non-carbon life on earth. Replacement of Zinc by Cadmium is  
  seen in marine algae during nutrient limiting conditions. Identify the reason for the substitution (3)  
  to occur. Studies conducted with Copper does not yield the same result. Justify.

  2A)   i) Tomato plants can be tall or short and have notched or smooth leaves. You cross a tall, smooth  
  leafed plant with a short, notched leafed plant. All of the progeny are tall, and notched leafed.  
  Identify the dominant and recessive traits?  
  
  ii) Mention the genotypes of the two true-breeding parents? Use the letters H or h to represent  
  the alleles of the height gene and the letters S or s to represent the alleles of the leaf gene.  
  
  iii) Two tall, notched F1 plants were crossed (self cross) to get 1600 F2 plants. What ratio of (4)  
  phenotype that you expect in the F2 generation? If you get 400 plants in F2, how many of these  
  will be homozygous recessive for both traits?  
  
  iv) You cross an F1 Plant with a double homozygous recessive plant and get 1600 plants in F2  
  generation. Give the types of the F2 plants that you will see. Give the genotype, phenotype and  
  the number of each of F2 classes generated.  
  (1+1+1+1 = 4 marks)  
  
  2B)   Carefully analyse the following pedigree, filled symbols represent the affected individuals.  
  
  
  (3)  
  
  
  i) What is the most likely mode of inheritance for this pedigree?  
  ii) State the genotypes of individuals # 1-5 in the following table using the letter "A". Use the  
  uppercase letter to represent the dominant allele and lowercase letter to represent the recessive  
  allele.  
  iii) If individuals #2 and #3 have another son what are the chances that this son will be affected?  
  
  2C)   In cattle, hornless (P) is dominant over horned (p). A hornless bull is mated to three cows, A, B,

  calf is produced. With cow C, which is hornless, a horned calf is produced. What are the           (3)  
  genotypes of the four parents (Cows A, B, C and Bull). Justify

  4A)          Sickle cell disease (SCD) describes a group of blood conditions that affect hemoglobin in RBCs.  
  Hemoglobin helps RBCs deliver oxygen throughout the body. SCD causes changes in the  
  hemoglobin molecule that can affect the shape and function of RBCs. While this condition can  
  negatively affect RBCs and cause potentially life-changing symptoms, certain types of SCD may  
  offer protection against malaria.                                                               (3)  
  i) What is the link between sickle cell anemia and malaria?  
  ii) How Does Sickle Cell Protect Against Malaria?  
  iii) Why does the Sickle Cell Trait Remain in the Human Population?
